name: SOUTH SUDAN

flag.title: South Sudan Flag
flag.note: 3 stripes, blue triangle with gold star

lead: South Sudan became the world's newest country on 9 July 2011. Nearly 99% of voters chose to break away from Sudan. The White Nile winds through huge papyrus swamps. Over 60 peoples speak their own languages.
geo: South Sudan lies on a flat basin drained by the White Nile. In the wet season, the Sudd swamp grows bigger than Belgium. It is a maze of papyrus reeds and floating islands.
In the south-east, the land climbs to cool, forested hills. Mount Kinyeti reaches 3,187 m. Six countries border South Sudan: Sudan, Ethiopia, Kenya, Uganda, DR Congo and Central African Republic.
animals: The shoebill is a bird with a huge shoe-shaped beak. It can gulp a whole lungfish (a fish with lungs).
Each year, around a million white-eared kob (an antelope) cross the Boma-Badingilo plains. It is one of the biggest animal migrations on Earth.
culture: The Dinka are South Sudan's largest group. They are devoted cattle-keepers. A family's herd is its bank and its wedding gift. Young men know their favourite ox by its horns and coat.
Music and wrestling fill celebrations. Women wear stacks of beaded necklaces. Some men mark their foreheads with V-shaped scars.
history: South Sudan's people fought for freedom for over 50 years. Sudan became independent in 1956, and southern leaders were left out. A long civil war cost over a million lives.
Peace came in 2005. On 9 July 2011, South Sudan raised a new flag with a golden star. It became Africa's 54th nation.
wows: South Sudan is the world's youngest country, born on 9 July 2011.
The Sudd swamp grows bigger than England in the rainy season.
About 75% of the old Sudan's oil lies under South Sudan.
The Boma kob migration may include a million animals, rivalling the famous Serengeti.
Over 60 peoples live here and speak about 60 languages.
Mount Kinyeti's forests feel like another world from the hot Nile plains.
The shoebill stands 1.5 m tall and belongs to a bird family of its own.

myths.fact: The Nile flows north. Its water starts far south, near Lake Victoria, and reaches Egypt last.

myths.myth: Ancient Egyptian paper came from tree bark
myths.fact: Papyrus paper came from the stems of a tall reed. Huge beds of it still grow in the Sudd.
